question.problem:
The table below gives the values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p,$ where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. Find the value of $z$ such that $P(Z\le z)=0.75.$

| $\,p\,$ | $0.65$ | $0.70$ | $0.75$ | $0.80$ | $0.85$ | $0.90$ | $0.95$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,0.3853\,$ | $\,0.5244\,$ | $\,0.6745\,$ | $\,0.8416\,$ | $\,1.0364\,$ | $\,1.2816\,$ | $\,1.6449\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
First, we express the given information in terms of $Φ:$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\le z) & =0.75 \\ Φ(z) & =0.75\end{aligned}
$$

So, we are looking for the value of $z$ such that

$$
z={Φ}^{-1}(0.75).
$$

We look for the column in the table that corresponds to $p=0.75,$ and we find that

$$
p=0.75\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(p)=0.6745.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
z={Φ}^{-1}(0.75)=0.6745.
$$
